findings.evidence: const client = new Client({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
findings.explanation: DATABASE_URL is read and passed straight into `new Client()` with no existence check first. Every other DB-backed factory in this codebase (core/admin/reader.js:126-130, core/admin/shop-writes.js:220-222, core/storage/postgres-adapter.js:243-245) guards with `if (!databaseUrl) throw ...` before connecting, and even this same file does the check two call sites earlier (wizard-routes.js:220 `if (process.env.DATABASE_URL) { ... }`). Here, if DATABASE_URL is unset, `client.connect()` falls back to libpq's PG* env vars / localhost defaults and fails with an opaque ECONNREFUSED/auth error instead of a clear 'DATABASE_URL is required' message — or worse, silently connects to whatever Postgres the PGHOST/PGUSER defaults resolve to.

findings.evidence: const dbClient = new (Client || loadPgClient())({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
findings.explanation: Same pattern as line 1343: process.env.DATABASE_URL is used directly to construct a pg Client with no guard for it being missing/undefined, inconsistent with the fail-fast `if (!databaseUrl) throw new Error(...)` guard used by every other Postgres-backed service factory in core/admin/*.js. A missing DATABASE_URL here surfaces as a generic connection failure deep in this handler rather than a clear startup/config error.
